senses.gloss: ऋश्य a. [ऋश्-कर्मणि-क्यप्] To be killed.

ऋश्य + .{@-श्यः@} A white-footed antelope; ऋश्यो न तृप्यन्नवपानमा गहि
 Rv. 8. 4. 10. वराहमृश्य पृषतं महारुरुम् Rām. 2. 52. 102.
ऋष्यः [ऋष्-क्यप्] —1 A white-footed antelope. see ऋश्य.

ऋश्य + .{@-श्यम्@} Killing, hurt, violation.
.━{@Comp.@}: ऋश्यकेतुः, ऋश्यकेतनः, ऋश्यदः, ऋश्यपद्, ऋश्यसूकः

ऋष्यः + .{@-ष्यम्@} A kind of leprosy.
.━{@Comp.@}: ऋष्याङ्कः, ऋष्यकेतनः, ऋष्यकेतुः, ऋष्यगता, ऋष्यगन्धा, ऋष्यजिह्वम्, ऋष्यप्रोक्ता, ऋष्यमूकः, ऋष्यशृङ्गः

ऋश्य + -केतुः, -केतनः
—1 N. of Aniruddha, son of Pradyumna.
—2 N. of the god of love.
ऋष्यः + -अङ्कः, -केतनः, -केतुः N. of Aniruddha.

ऋश्य + -केतुः, -केतनः
—1 N. of Aniruddha, son of Pradyumna.
—2 N. of the god of love.
ऋष्यः + -अङ्कः, -केतनः, -केतुः N. of Aniruddha.
ऋश्य + -दः a pit for catching antelopes.
ऋश्य + -पद् a. having the feet of an antelope.
ऋश्य + -सूकः N. of a mountain.

ऋषिः + -ऋणम् A debt
[]
 due to Ṛṣis.
ऋष्यः + -अङ्कः, -केतनः, -केतुः N. of Aniruddha.
ऋष्यः + -गता the plant Asparagus Racemosus (= ऋष्यप्रोक्ता).
ऋष्यः + -गन्धा the plant ऋक्षगन्धा.
ऋष्यः + -जिह्वम् a kind of leprosy.
ऋष्यः + -प्रोक्ता N. of several plants; शूकशिंबी, अतिबला, शतावरी.

ऋष्यः + -मूकः a mountain near the lake Pampā which formed the temporary
 abode of Rāma with the monkey-chief Sugrīva; ऋष्यसूकस्तु पम्पायाः
 पुरस्तात् पुष्पितद्रुमः.

ऋष्यः + -शृङ्गः N. of a sage. [He
[]
 was the son of Vibhāṇḍaka. According to mythical account he was born
 of a female deer, and had a small horn on his forehead, and hence called
 ‘Ṛṣyaśṛnga’, or ‘deer-horned’. He was brought up in the forest by
 his father, and he saw no other human being till he nearly reached his
 manhood. When a great drought well nigh devastated the country of Aṅga,
 its king Lomapāda, at the advice of Brāhmaṇas, caused Ṛṣyaśṛṅga
 to be brought to him by means of a number of damsels, and gave his daughter Śantā
[]
 (adopted by him, her real father being Daśaratha) in marriage to him,
 who being greatly pleased caused copious showers of rain to fall in his
 kingdom. It was this sage that performed for king Daśaratha the sacrifice
 which brought about the birth or Rāma and his three brothers].
ऋष्यकः A painted or white-footed antelope.
